# Configuration reference

`.contractguard.yaml` (or `.yml`, `.json`) is found in the current directory or a parent, up to the git root. Unknown keys are errors, reported with the file, line and column. Paths are relative to the configuration file.

Editors with YAML language support validate and complete the file with the published schema:

```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=./node_modules/@zainkhan-bit/contractguard-app/schemas/config.v1.json
version: 1
```

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `$schema` | string | JSON Schema URL for editor support; ignored by ContractGuard. |
| `version` | `1` | Configuration format version. Always 1. |
| `specs` | list of object | The comparisons to run, each with a base and a candidate. |
| `specs[].id` | string | Name of this comparison; also the report file name. |
| `specs[].candidate` | string | The new version: a path, git:&lt;ref>:&lt;path>, snapshot:&lt;file> or an https URL. |
| `specs[].base` | string | The version to compare against, e.g. git:origin/main:openapi.yaml or git:@base:openapi.yaml in CI. |
| `compatibility` | object | Compatibility model. |
| `compatibility.perspective` | `provider-backward` | Whose compatibility is checked. provider-backward (default): can existing consumers keep working against the new provider? |
| `policy` | object | When the check fails. |
| `policy.failOn` | list of `breaking`, `potentially-breaking`, `undetermined`, `non-breaking`, `informational` | Classifications that fail the check. Default: [breaking]. |
| `policy.minSeverity` | `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, `info` | Findings below this severity never fail the check. Default: low. |
| `policy.undetermined` | `fail`, `review`, `ignore` | Findings whose compatibility cannot be decided: fail the check, show for review (default) or hide. |
| `analysis` | object | How changes are classified, and resource limits. |
| `analysis.strictResponseValidation` | boolean | Assume consumers reject unknown response properties (new response properties become potentially breaking). Default: false. |
| `analysis.constraintTightening` | `potentially-breaking`, `breaking` | Classification of tighter request constraints such as a lower maximum or a stricter pattern. Default: potentially-breaking. |
| `analysis.responseEnumAdditions` | `potentially-breaking`, `non-breaking`, `breaking` | Classification of new enum values in responses. Default: potentially-breaking. |
| `analysis.removedRequestParameters` | `non-breaking`, `potentially-breaking` | Classification of removed optional request parameters that consumers may still send. Default: non-breaking. |
| `analysis.closedResponseAdditions` | `potentially-breaking`, `breaking` | Classification of new properties in responses declared closed (additionalProperties: false). Default: potentially-breaking. |
| `analysis.honorExtensibleEnum` | boolean | Treat x-extensible-enum (and enums marked extensible) as open: new values are non-breaking. Default: true. |
| `analysis.includeEquivalentChanges` | boolean | Report changes that only alter the representation, e.g. nullable: true ↔ type: [.., null]. Default: false. |
| `analysis.allowInvalidSpec` | boolean | Continue past specification errors; the run is marked degraded. Default: false. |
| `analysis.limits` | object | Resource limits; inputs above them are rejected or reported as undetermined, never silently passed. |
| `analysis.limits.maxDocumentBytes` | integer or string | Largest single document, e.g. 20MB (default). |
| `analysis.limits.maxTotalBytes` | integer or string | Total size of all documents of one side. Default: 100MB. |
| `analysis.limits.maxDocuments` | integer | Documents reachable through $ref per side. Default: 5000. |
| `analysis.limits.maxDepth` | integer | Maximum nesting depth of a document. Default: 256. |
| `analysis.limits.maxRefHops` | integer | Maximum length of a $ref chain. Default: 64. |
| `analysis.limits.maxSchemaPairs` | integer | Schema pairs compared before the rest becomes undetermined. Default: 250000. |
| `analysis.limits.timeoutMs` | integer | Time limit per spec in milliseconds. Default: 120000. |
| `rules` | object | Turn rules off, change their classification or severity, or silence specific findings. |
| `rules.disable` | list of string | Rule ids to turn off completely. |
| `rules.overrides` | map | Per-rule settings keyed by rule id: `classification` (when the rule allows it), `severity`, `options`. |
| `rules.ignore` | list of object | Accepted findings. Each entry needs `rule` or `fingerprint` and a `reason`; suppressed findings stay visible in reports. |
| `rules.ignore[].rule` | string | Silence this rule (optionally narrowed by operation and path). |
| `rules.ignore[].fingerprint` | string | Silence exactly one finding (fingerprints are stable across runs). |
| `rules.ignore[].operation` | string | Limit the ignore to one operation, e.g. "GET /users/{id}". |
| `rules.ignore[].path` | string | Schema path the ignore applies to, e.g. $.items[].name. |
| `rules.ignore[].reason` | string | Why this is acceptable. Shown in reports. |
| `rules.ignore[].expires` | string | YYYY-MM-DD after which the ignore stops applying (warned 30 days ahead). |
| `filters` | object | Which operations are checked. |
| `filters.include` | list of string | Only check operations matching one of these, e.g. "*:/public/**". |
| `filters.exclude` | list of string | Skip operations matching one of these, e.g. "*:/internal/**" or "POST:/admin/*". |
| `filters.excludeTags` | list of string | Skip operations with any of these tags. |
| `filters.excludeExtensions` | list of string | Skip operations where one of these extensions is true, e.g. x-internal. |
| `references` | object | Where `$ref` may point. Remote references are off by default. |
| `references.root` | string | Local $ref targets must be inside this directory. Default: the git repository root. |
| `references.allowRemote` | boolean | Allow http(s) $refs to allowedHosts. Default: false. In CI it also needs --allow-remote-references. |
| `references.allowedHosts` | list of string | Exact host names remote $refs may load from (no wildcards). |
| `references.allowedSchemes` | list of `https`, `http` | URL schemes for remote $refs. Default: [https]. |
| `references.fetchTimeoutMs` | integer | Timeout per remote document. Default: 10000. |
| `references.maxRemoteBytes` | integer or string | Largest remote document. Default: 5MB. |
| `report` | object | Report formats and files. |
| `report.formats` | list of `console`, `markdown`, `json`, `sarif` | Report formats. Default: [console]; in CI [console, json]. Files are written to outputDir. |
| `report.outputDir` | string | Directory for report files, relative to this file. Default: .contractguard/reports. |
| `report.groupBy` | `cause`, `operation` | Group findings by root cause (default) or by operation. |
| `report.deterministic` | boolean | Omit timestamps so reports are byte-identical across runs. Default: false. |

Sizes accept `512KB`, `20MB`, `1GB` (binary units; `MiB` spellings too) or a number of bytes.
